info.timeAllocation:

info.description:
This course offers an essential guide to ethically navigating the complex legal terrain of media by addressing key issues such as the rights and liability of communicator/ media maker/ media user in classical and internet-based media; the intellectual property issues; and legal principles in press and publication.
In this course, students will explore the risks and rights associated with media use and learn to manage intellectual property issues in this evolving landscape with an ethical approach. Upon completing this course, students are expected to achieve a comprehensive grasp of press and media law, journalism ethics, intellectual property rights, and communication responsibilities. They will learn to understand and apply ethical principles within various contexts, including press, communication, politics, and society.
Students will also enhance their ability to critically analyze media laws and apply them to real-world situations. They will be skilled in constructing and communicating well-founded legal arguments with an ethical approach. Finally, the course will instill a professional, ethical, and responsible attitude towards media-related activities, preparing students to uphold the highest standards in their future media engagements.

Working in group
Presenting, Reviewing, Discussing, working in group as stipulated in a standard Constructivism slot

Students will explore how AI can be used to search for and analyze case studies related to restricting access to social media. They will define filtering criteria, evaluate the results, and present one selected case for class discussion.

Instructions:
1. Use AI tools to search for real-world case studies involving restrictions on social media access (e.g., government bans, school policies, parental controls).
2. Define filtering criteria for AI to select relevant and high-quality case studies. Suggested criteria:
- Target population (e.g., minors, students, employees)
- Type of restriction (e.g., time limits, platform bans, age verification)
- Geographic location
- Legal or ethical implications
- Measurable outcomes (e.g., impact on mental health, academic performance)
3. Select one case study and prepare a short presentation that includes:
- Background and context
- Key stakeholders involved
- Type of restriction and how it was implemented
- Outcomes and controversies
- Questions for class discussion

Unit 3 - Intellectual property - Introduction and fundamental knowledge
Intellectual Property: The Need for Reform
Use AI tools to identify and analyze key reasons why current intellectual property (IP) law frameworks may be outdated or insufficient in the digital age.
sessions.studentMaterials:
Slides; Syllabus, and other materials suggested by Lecturer

sessions.studentTasks:
Reading:
1. Textbook: Intellectual Property Rights for Engineers - Chapter 1 - Introduction

Working in group
Presenting, Reviewing, Discussing, working in group as stipulated in a standard Constructivism slot

AI Practice:
Students will use AI tools to identify and analyze key reasons why current intellectual property (IP) law frameworks may be outdated or insufficient in the digital age. They will explore global perspectives, emerging technologies, and societal shifts that challenge traditional IP models, The guidance as following:
1. Work individually or in pairs.
2. Use AI tools (e.g., Copilot, ChatGPT, Perplexity) to research arguments and expert opinions on why IP law needs reform.
3. Identify at least 3 key reasons for change. Suggested angles:
- Rise of generative AI and blurred authorship
- Global digital distribution vs. territorial IP rights
- Biotech and data ownership complexities
- Remix culture and user-generated content
- Access to knowledge vs. copyright monopolies
4. For each reason, students should:
- Describe the issue clearly
- Provide a real-world example or case
- Explain how current IP law fails to address it
- Suggest a possible direction for reform
- Prepare a short 5-minute presentation or infographic to share findings with the class.

2. Social Media and the Law A Guidebook for Communication Students and Professionals - Chapter 4 - Intellectual property

Textbook
Working in group
Presenting, Reviewing, Discussing, working in group as stipulated in a standard Constructivism slot.

AI Activity:
Students will use AI tools to simulate a legal defense in response to a copyright infringement accusation. They will explore relevant legal concepts, precedents, and exceptions (e.g., fair use) to build a reasoned argument.

1. Scenario Setup
Each student (or pair) receives a fictional situation in which they are accused of violating copyright. Example scenarios:
- Used copyrighted music in a YouTube video
- Quoted a large portion of a published article in a blog post
- Shared a meme based on a copyrighted image
- Trained a personal AI model on copyrighted content
2. Research with AI Tools
Students use AI (e.g., Copilot, ChatGPT) to:
- Understand the copyright issue involved
- Identify possible exceptions or defenses (e.g., fair use, parody, educational use)
- Find similar real-world cases or legal precedents
- Draft a short defense argument (max 300 words)
3. Present Defense Argument Each student presents their defense to the class or in small groups. The presentation should include:
- Summary of the accusation
- Legal basis for their defense
- Supporting examples or precedents
- A closing statement
4. Optional Role Play
Assign classmates to play the role of “copyright holder” or “judge” to challenge or evaluate the defense.

Students will use AI tools to investigate real-world cases involving deceptive endorsements or unfair advertising practices. They will evaluate how these practices affect consumer trust, violate legal standards, and challenge ethical norms in digital marketing.
1. Form small groups (2–3 students).
2. Use AI tools (e.g., Copilot, ChatGPT, Perplexity) to research one real-world case involving deceptive advertising or misleading endorsements. Suggested cases:
- Influencers failing to disclose paid partnerships
- Fake reviews or testimonials on e-commerce platforms
- Misleading health claims in product ads
- Brand manipulation through virtual influencers
3. Analyze the case using the following framework:
- What happened? (Brief summary of the situation)
- What laws or guidelines were violated? (e.g., FTC Endorsement Guides, Lanham Act)
- How did it affect consumer trust or public perception?
- What could have been done differently?
- How can AI help detect or prevent such practices?
4. Prepare a short presentation (5–7 minutes) or infographic that includes:
- Case summary
- Legal and ethical analysis
- AI’s role in identifying or mitigating deceptive practices
- Recommendations for advertisers and platforms

AI activity
Students will investigate and analyze real-world case studies that demonstrate how organizations use social media for strategic communication purposes such as branding, crisis management, influencer engagement, and audience listening.
1. Group Formation & Topic Assignment
Divide students into small groups (3–4 members).
Each group selects or is assigned a specific use case of social media in strategic communication:
- Brand storytelling
- Crisis communication
- Influencer marketing
- Social listening and sentiment analysis
- Viral campaigns and public engagement
2. Case Study Research
Students use AI tools and online sources to find a relevant case study. Examples include:
- Nike’s Colin Kaepernick campaign (brand activism)
- United Airlines passenger incident (crisis response)
- Fenty Beauty’s influencer strategy (inclusive marketing)
- ALS Ice Bucket Challenge (viral awareness campaign)
- Spotify Wrapped (personalized engagement)
3. Analysis Framework
Each group analyzes their case using this structure:
- Background: What happened? Who was involved?
- Strategic Goal: What was the communication objective?
- Social Media Tactics: Which platforms and strategies were used?
- Impact: What were the outcomes (positive/negative)?
- AI Insight: How could AI tools enhance or evaluate this strategy?
4. Presentation & Reflection
- Groups present their findings in a 7–10 minute presentation.
- Include visuals, social media screenshots, and AI-generated insights.
- End with a reflection: What lessons can future communicators learn?

Students will write an in-class essay that demonstrates their understanding of key legal principles related to either:

The essay question will be provided at the time of the test and will reflect a prominent, timely issue in one of the two areas above.

assessments.gradingGuide:
In class and home conducted from assinged topic until oral presentation
Students will work in groups of up to five members to implement this assignment. Each group will find a real legal case of foreign or domestic court about a litigation relating to press or the rights of persons on social media to present to the class under a form of debating.
Arguments to protect the rights/ benefits of involved party must be presented and the final decision (which is made by the judge) will also be presented after debating. Student must illustrate their opinions about the case to make the case more comprehensive and fairer.
Students follow below steps to successfully undertake the assignment:
Phase 1: Selecting case
- Research potential cases, legal databases, or news sources
- Identify the problem of the case, which can be improved. Ensure the case involves a court decision and legal arguments
- Submit a short proposal (1 paragraph) with:
- Case name and jurisdiction
- Summary of the issue
- Why it’s relevant to press or social media rights
Note: The proposal must be self-made by students

Phase 2: Case Analysis & Report Writing
Objective: Analyze the case and prepare a written report with legal reasoning and group opinions.
Identify the parties involved and their arguments
Summarize the legal claims (e.g., defamation, censorship, privacy violation)
Present the final court decision and reasoning
Develop arguments defending one party’s rights or benefits
Students can refer other resources by:
- Finding similar cases or precedents
- Analyzing public sentiment or media coverage
- Exploring ethical implications"
Write a group report including:
- Case summary
- Legal analysis
- Group’s position and justification
- Reflections on fairness and broader impact
Note: This report should be made by students themselves

Phase 3: Presentation & Debate (handling directly by student themselves)
Objective: Present the case and engage in a structured debate defending one party’s position.
"Prepare a 20-minute presentation:
- Case overview
- Legal arguments
- Group’s defense of one party
- Final court decision"
"Role-play debate:
- Assign one other team defends the presented team (may be plaintiff or defendant depending on the actual situation)
- Class or instructor acts as judge"
- Use visuals, quotes, or AI-generated insights to support arguments
assessments.note:
Each team will discuss in advance with the lecturer about the suitability of the case that they will present.

The mark will be given based on each student's performance, not on the whole group's. It means each student will get their own mark.

Group size: 5-6 members

Depending on the practical context, lecturer can design 1 more moot court and respectively devide the proportion of the group assignment grade.
